simple.meaning: אֲנַס (ʼănaç) is a Hebrew action word meaning “figuratively, to distress.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 4:6. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֲנַס (H598) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אֲנַס (ʼănaç) / H598 is traced through Daniel 4:6 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H598. anas [ אֲנַס ] verb oppress (Biblical Hebrew [late] constrain ); — Pe`al Participle לָ֑ךְ אָנֵס Dan 4:6 .
